L. J. LeBlanc, E. K. Morlok, W. P. Pierskalla (1975). An efficient approach to solving the road network equilibrium traffic assignment problem. Transportation Research 9(5), 309-318.

description: The Sioux Falls network of LeBlanc, Morlok and Pierskalla (1975), with the paper's daily flows multiplied by 100 (so 0.1 of the daily flows) and capacities computed for B = 0.15; the repository's readme notes that it is not a realistic network. From Transportation Networks for Research, the traffic assignment test networks that continue H. Bar-Gera's TNTP collection, read from the repository at commit d1639b4ef218 in the TNTP format: the network file's links are directed edges of type link carrying capacity, length, freeFlowTime, b, power, speed, toll, linkType, and every node is a zone; each origin-destination entry of the trip table is a node of type commodity carrying its demand, joined by an origin edge and a destination edge to its two zones, zero entries included as the file lists them. The node coordinate files are not read. The best known equilibrium link flows are in the repository's SiouxFalls_flow.tntp, which this entry lists as a source and does not merge.
